statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 12% (low), Stress 37% (moderate), Confidence 87% (high). Shared assessment for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON. Conditional risk is concentrated in a narrow 13:30-15:00 UTC band spanning the U.S. cash open, the Richmond Fed survey and the Williams and Jefferson remarks; that band is published as the danger window instead of the whole session. A lighter second checkpoint sits at the 17:00 UTC 2-year auction and Barkin remarks, and a third in the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping. The reading would change on observed persistent one-way structure: shallow or absent pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, NQ holding near a session extreme, or aligned yields, VIX, oil, semiconductors and breadth confirming a single direction.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold mid-range and slightly below settlement with both overnight extremes rejected; a 14.67 VIX, easing 2Y and 10Y yields and a fifth consecutive lower oil session keep tail risk low into the U.S. cash open
body: Monday closed with the Nasdaq-100 cash index at a record 30,482.35, up 2.83% inside a 29,933.22-30,557.33 day range, as an AI and semiconductor rally lifted the Nasdaq Composite 2.26% to a record 27,122.09 and the S&P 500 1.49% to 7,764.70. Leadership was narrow but powerful: AMD rose about 10% to a record and became the fourth U.S. chipmaker worth $1 trillion, Intel gained about 12%, Qualcomm more than 9%, Meta about 11% on the reception of its Muse AI app, and the PHLX semiconductor index rose 4.29%. Overnight the NQ Dec-26 contract traded a 30,670.00-30,916.50 range against a 30,784.75 prior settlement and now sits near 30,750-30,757, down about 0.1%. Two independent quote sources agree on that level. Price holding the middle of the overnight range after both extremes were rejected is direct evidence that retracement is functioning in both directions, which is the main reason Tail stays low despite the size of Monday's advance. Cross-asset evidence points the same way rather than amplifying. The VIX is 14.67, down 1.35% from a 14.87 close and confined to a 14.64-14.95 band. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.93% and the 2-year 4.74%, both a couple of basis points lower, with the 5-year at 4.81% and the 30-year at 5.27%; easing yields remove the tightening channel that normally accompanies a one-way equity trend. WTI is $90.44, down 2.09%, and Brent $98.67, a fifth consecutive lower session, after Reuters reported a senior Iranian official saying Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the United States eases military pressure and lifts its blockade, with a proposal delivered through mediators on 16 September. That is a de-escalation vector rather than a discontinuity, and Washington has not publicly accepted the conditions, so it is treated as a live two-sided headline risk. The scheduled load today is moderate and clustered: the Richmond Fed manufacturing survey at 14:00 UTC, Williams at 14:05 and Jefferson at 14:20, then the 2-year note auction and Barkin at 17:00. None of these is an automatic block, but the rate path is genuinely live after the Fed's move to a 3.75-4.00% target range, so speaker headlines can move yields and the AI complex together. The shared Finviz cross-asset context was not used as evidence this run: its payload is about two hours old, its collection status is partial, and its futures and calendar sections are unavailable, so it fails the freshness and completeness bar and the assessment rests entirely on independently fetched primary sources. The dominant mode is normal. None of the Tail amplifiers is present: there is no persistent directional efficiency, no sequence of failed retracements, no repeated extension and no holding near a session extreme. Stress at 37 reflects the record-close starting point, narrow leadership, the clustered speaker block and tomorrow's high-impact flash PMIs. Confidence at 87 reflects current verified levels for the index, futures, volatility, yields and oil, a cross-checked event calendar and a verified geopolitical story.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours contain a complete set of 24 published hourly assessments. Tail built steadily through Monday's U.S. session as the index trended to a record close, peaking at 33 with Stress at 57 in the 19:00 UTC hour, which mapped to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES from 14:00 through 19:00 UTC. After the cash close the trend-up characterisation gave way to a normal, two-way regime: Tail fell to 23 by 20:00 UTC and to 14 by 21:00 UTC, then held an 11-13 band through the entire Asian and European overnight, with Stress between 32 and 39 and Confidence between 85 and 87. Every hour from 21:00 UTC onward mapped to EA_ON, and the final six hours sat at Tail 12-13 with Stress 36-38. Nothing in that sequence has been revised with later information.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook keeps Tail inside a 10-18 band, so every forecast hour maps to EA_ON. Conditional risk is front-loaded into the 13:30-15:00 UTC band covering the cash open, the Richmond Fed survey and the Williams and Jefferson remarks, where Tail peaks at 18 and Stress at 48. Lighter secondary checkpoints follow at the 17:00 UTC 2-year auction with Barkin, and in the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour that carried Monday's highest Tail reading. From the 20:00 UTC cash close the path assumes liquidity drains and Tail decays to a 10-11 overnight floor, then rebuilds gradually to 14 at the end of the window as Wednesday's high-impact S&P Global flash PMIs at 13:45 UTC come into view. Confidence decays from 87 to 79 across the window because live price-path evidence beyond the current hour is projected rather than observed.
